python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

img = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(img).astype(float)  # (200, 1000, 3)
h, w, _ = a.shape

# Treat each column as one sample
cols = a.mean(axis=0)  # (1000, 3)
r, g, b = cols[:,0], cols[:,1], cols[:,2]

mx = cols.max(axis=1); mn = cols.min(axis=1)
sat = np.where(mx>0, (mx-mn)/np.maximum(mx,1e-6), 0)
lum = cols.mean(axis=1)
hue = np.degrees(np.arctan2(np.sqrt(3)*(g-b), 2*r-g-b)) % 360

print("Global mean RGB:", cols.mean(axis=0).round(1))
print("Mean luminance: %.1f  Median luminance: %.1f" % (lum.mean(), np.median(lum)))
print("Mean saturation: %.3f  Max saturation: %.3f" % (sat.mean(), sat.max()))
print("Fraction of columns with lum < 20 (near black): %.3f" % (lum < 20).mean())
print("Fraction with lum < 40: %.3f" % (lum < 40).mean())
print("Fraction with sat > 0.35: %.3f" % (sat > 0.35).mean())

# Hue histogram (weighted, only for non-dark pixels)
mask = lum > 30
hb, edges = np.histogram(hue[mask], bins=[0,20,40,60,80,100,120,140,160,180,200,220,240,260,280,300,320,340,360], weights=lum[mask])
tot = hb.sum()
names = ['red0-20','20-40','yellow40-60','60-80','80-100 green','100-120','120-140','140-160','160-180 cyan','180-200','200-220 blue','220-240','240-260','260-280','280-300 magenta','300-320','320-340','340-360']
print("\nHue distribution (weighted by luminance, lum>30):")
for name, v in zip(names, hb):
    if v/tot > 0.01: print("  %s: %.1f%%" % (name, 100*v/tot))

# Segment the strip into 10 acts, print stats
print("\nSegment stats (10 equal parts):")
for i in range(10):
    s, e = int(i*w/10), int((i+1)*w/10)
    c = cols[s:e]; L = lum[s:e]; S = sat[s:e]
    print("  seg %d (t=%3d-%3d%%): RGB=%s lum=%5.1f sat=%.3f darkfrac=%.2f" % (
        i, i*10, (i+1)*10, c.mean(axis=0).round(0).astype(int), L.mean(), S.mean(), (L<20).mean()))
EOF

part.text: Key findings so far: the barcode is very dark (mean luminance ~49/255), dominated by warm yellow-brown hues (~80% of luminance in the yellow/orange-brown bands), almost no blue (2.3%), only 3.4% green, low saturation, and a long black tail (~86% of the final tenth is black — end credits). from PIL import Image
img = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w, h = img.size
# Upscale 3x vertical for visibility and crop into 5 horizontal sections, each resized to 1000x200
for i in range(5):
    s, e = int(i*w/5), int((i+1)*w/5)
    crop = img.crop((s, 0, e, h)).resize((1000, 200), Image.NEAREST)
    crop.save(f'sec{i}.png')
print("saved")
EOF
